services.name: Groww
services.note: Save an access token (they end daily at 6:00 AM IST). A saved TOTP token or API key can only make access tokens (POST /v1/token/api/access), and that call hands the box a real one, which Keystub refuses in requests. The SDK has no base-URL variable: for quick start, set groww.domain to GROWW_BASE_URL after GrowwAPI(GROWW_ACCESS_TOKEN). The live feed (socket-api.groww.in) uses its own socket token and isn't covered.

services.name: Cloudflare
services.note: API tokens only; the legacy global key (X-Auth-Key plus email) isn't supported.

services.name: Vercel
services.note: The Vercel CLI rejects "-" in tokens, so it gets the compact form.

services.name: Google Gemini
services.note: The OpenAI-compatible endpoints take the key in Authorization: Bearer, which also works.

services.name: Vercel AI Gateway
services.note: The token goes in Authorization as a bearer token, as the OpenAI SDK and the AI SDK send it; the Anthropic SDK and Claude Code need ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (x-api-key).

services.name: Z.AI
services.note: General keys use /api/paas/v4; GLM Coding Plan keys use /api/coding/paas/v4, or /api/anthropic for Anthropic-style clients, which need ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (x-api-key).

services.name: MiniMax
services.note: A key works only in its own region: api.minimax.io (and api-uw.minimax.io for speech) internationally, api.minimax.cn in China. For the /anthropic endpoint set ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (x-api-key).

services.name: xAI
services.note: REST API. The official Python SDK uses gRPC, which needs the proxy, not quick start.

services.name: Together AI
services.note: SDK 1.x calls api.together.xyz; 3.x calls api.together.ai.

services.name: Fireworks AI
services.note: No quick start: with FIREWORKS_BASE_URL set the SDK drops the /inference path.

services.name: Parallel
services.note: The API takes the key in x-api-key; the MCP server (mcp.parallel.ai) takes it as a bearer token, which is swapped where it is.

services.name: Firecrawl
services.note: The JS SDK's crawl watcher sends the key as a WebSocket subprotocol, which Keystub refuses; without it the SDK polls.

services.name: Bright Data
services.note: The REST API only; proxy zones and the Browser API use their own username and password.

services.name: Replicate
services.note: No quick start: REPLICATE_BASE_URL means the bare host to the Python SDK 1.x but includes /v1 for the CLI and SDK 2.x.

services.name: fal
services.note: A key made of an ID and a secret is saved as ID:SECRET. The Python client retries on falrun.com, listed too. Realtime and CDN uploads use short-lived tokens, not the key.

services.name: Supabase Management API
services.note: Personal access tokens (sbp_…). Not the per-project data API (*.supabase.co), which uses anon and service keys.

services.name: Upstash Box
services.note: The key goes in X-Box-Api-Key, as @upstash/box sends it. Only the default region host is listed.

services.name: Upstash QStash
services.note: Each region has its own token, so a multi-region setup needs a saved key per region. The ?qstash_token= form isn't covered.

services.name: Pinecone
services.note: Index hosts vary per index, hence the wildcard; no quick start for them.

services.name: Railway
services.note: Account and workspace tokens. Project tokens (RAILWAY_TOKEN) use a Project-Access-Token header and aren't supported.

services.name: Fly.io
services.note: Save the whole token as fly tokens create prints it, FlyV1 prefix included: Fly takes it as a bearer token, prefix and all. Covers the Machines API and the GraphQL API; fly deploy also pushes images to registry.fly.io, which isn't covered.

services.name: RunPod
services.note: REST, GraphQL and serverless endpoints, plus load-balancing endpoints at <endpoint-id>.api.runpod.ai. The SDKs don't read RUNPOD_API_KEY themselves; the docs' examples pass it in.

services.name: Browserbase
services.note: The REST API only: connecting a browser with ?apiKey= in the URL isn't covered; use the session's connectUrl.

services.name: Sentry
services.note: Auth tokens (Bearer). Event ingest uses the DSN, not this token.

services.name: Axiom
services.note: Personal tokens also need X-Axiom-Org-Id, which isn't a secret.

services.name: Laminar
services.note: Traces over OTLP/HTTP on 443; the SDK's default OTLP/gRPC on port 8443 doesn't go through Keystub, so force HTTP.

services.name: Braintrust
services.note: The SDK signs in at www.braintrust.dev first, then uses the org's API host. Self-hosted data planes aren't covered.

services.name: GitLab
services.note: Personal, project and group tokens, in PRIVATE-TOKEN or Authorization: Bearer. CI job tokens (JOB-TOKEN) aren't supported.

services.name: npm registry
services.note: npm reads NPM_TOKEN through an .npmrc line: //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}.

services.name: Linear
services.note: Personal API keys are sent raw, without Bearer.

services.name: Clerk
services.note: The Backend API with a secret key; publishable keys aren't secrets and stay as they are.

services.name: Slack
services.note: The token must be in the Authorization header; a token in a form field isn't swapped.

services.name: Twilio
services.note: Basic auth: the account or API key SID stays real as the user name; the proxy token is the password. Apps that check webhook signatures with TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN need the real token for that, so don't run them under keystub run.

services.name: Intercom
services.note: A workspace lives in one region, so its token works on one of the three hosts.

services.name: Postmark
services.note: Server tokens only; account-token endpoints (X-Postmark-Account-Token) aren't supported.

services.name: MailerLite
services.note: The new API only; the classic API (api.mailerlite.com, X-MailerLite-ApiKey) isn't covered.

services.name: Algolia
services.note: The application ID (x-algolia-application-id) isn't secret and stays real.

services.name: Azure OpenAI
services.note: Resource hosts vary, hence the wildcards; no quick start. Microsoft Entra ID tokens are short-lived and not covered. Other Azure AI services on these hosts that take the key in Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key aren't covered.

services.name: Deepgram
services.note: API keys go as Token, not Bearer. Browser WebSockets pass the key as a subprotocol, which isn't swapped; server-side SDKs send the header.

services.name: AssemblyAI
services.note: The key is sent raw in Authorization, without Bearer. Temporary streaming tokens in the ?token= query aren't swapped.

services.name: Cartesia
services.note: Browser clients that pass the key in the query string aren't covered.

services.name: Voyage AI
services.note: Keys issued by MongoDB Atlas (al-…) go to ai.mongodb.com.

services.name: Tavily
services.note: Old SDKs that put api_key in the request body, and the hosted MCP server's key in the URL, aren't swapped.

services.name: LangSmith
services.note: Regional hosts (eu.api.smith.langchain.com and others) are covered by the wildcard; self-hosted instances aren't. No quick start, since the regions don't share a host.

services.name: Langfuse
services.note: Basic auth: the public key (LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, pk-lf-…) stays real as the user name; the proxy token is the password. Regions us., jp. and hipaa. are covered by the wildcard; no quick start, since the regions don't share a host.

services.name: Helicone
services.note: Covers the AI Gateway and the Helicone API. The older per-provider proxies (oai.helicone.ai and others) need a second key in Helicone-Auth and aren't covered.

services.name: Turso Platform API
services.note: Account-level platform token. Database tokens are the Turso database entry.

services.name: Turso database
services.note: A database token over HTTP (https:// URLs). libsql:// and WebSocket connections send the token inside the protocol, which isn't swapped.

services.name: Qdrant Cloud
services.note: A cluster's database key over REST (port 6333). gRPC (port 6334) and the Cloud Management API (apikey scheme) aren't covered.

services.name: Weaviate Cloud
services.note: REST only; the clients' gRPC connection isn't covered. Model provider keys in X-…-Api-Key headers must stay real.

services.name: Razorpay
services.note: Basic auth: the key ID (rzp_live_… or rzp_test_…) stays real as the user name; the proxy token is the password. Checking payment signatures uses the key secret locally, so that needs the real secret.

services.name: Paddle
services.note: Webhook signatures use a separate secret.

services.name: WorkOS
services.note: The SDK also sends the key as client_secret in the body of AuthKit code exchanges, which isn't swapped.

services.name: Mailgun
services.note: Basic auth: the fixed name api stays real as the user name; the proxy token is the password. Webhook signing keys and SMTP passwords are separate.

services.name: Discord
services.note: Bot tokens over the REST API. Bots on the gateway WebSocket send the token inside a message, which isn't swapped.

services.name: PostHog
services.note: The personal API key (phx_…) for the private API. The project key (phc_…) is public and stays real; ingestion hosts (us.i.posthog.com and others) aren't claimed, so capture calls and local flag evaluation there go out unchanged.

services.name: Datadog
services.note: Covers the API key, which is all that sending metrics, events, service checks and logs needs. Calls that also need the application key (DD-APPLICATION-KEY) send it real; a stand-in there is refused.

services.name: Mixpanel
services.note: Basic auth: the service account's user name stays real as the user name; the proxy token is the password. The project token for tracking is public and stays real.

services.name: Segment Public API
services.note: A workspace token for managing sources and destinations. Tracking write keys aren't covered: the SDKs also put them in the request body.

services.name: HubSpot
services.note: Private app access tokens (pat-…). Developer API keys go in the query string and aren't covered.

services.name: Atlassian (Jira, Confluence)
services.note: Basic auth: the account email stays real as the user name; the proxy token is the password. Scoped API tokens go through api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudId}.

services.name: Shopify
services.note: Admin API access tokens (shpat_…). Storefront tokens use other headers, and the app's client secret (token exchange, webhook HMAC) isn't covered.

services.name: Cloudinary
services.note: Basic auth: the API key stays real as the user name; the proxy token is the password. The SDKs sign uploads locally with the secret, so SDK uploads need the real secret; Admin API calls and unsigned Basic-auth uploads work. CLOUDINARY_URL holds both halves and isn't set.
